newsitem.title: UK: Energy Group in talks with PacifiCorp.
newsitem.headline: Energy Group in talks with PacifiCorp.

text.p: Energy Group Plc, the UK electricity and U.S. coal interests group spun off from conglomerate Hanson in February, said on Tuesday it was in talks with U.S. firm PacifiCorp which may lead to a recommended cash offer for Energy Group.
It said in a statement any offer would be expected to be at a premium of about 20 percent to today's closing price of 5.80 pounds ($9.49) per share on the London Stock Exchange.

Energy Group said it would not now be announcing its interim results for the six months to March 31 until the outcome of these talks was settled. It had been scheduled to release first-half figures on Thursday.
It said in the statement a further announcement, which would include the results, would be made "as soon as practicable".

The group, Britain's biggest electricity distributor, only made its stock exchange debut on February 24. Operating profits were 138 million pounds, up 38 percent, in the three months to December 31, when the company was still part of Hanson.
It owns regional electricity supplier Eastern Electricity and is the country's fourth biggest generator. Energy Group also owns the U.S. coal business Peabody Resources Ltd.
